es: Recuperar lo que se omite o se sustituye en réplicas rápidas (I'd love to, So have I, Neither did she, I hope so, I'm afraid not) y deducir qué piensa quien responde.

teaching.en: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to, but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”
teaching.es: Para rechazar una invitación con cortesía, empieza con calidez: «Me encantaría, pero me temo que estoy desbordado de trabajo hasta el viernes.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd love to omite el verbo que ya se dijo (come): solo queda to. Después del but llega la razón.
segments: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to,
but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”
teaching.audioText: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to, but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”

teaching.en: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”
teaching.es: «Estoy absolutamente agotado después de ese viaje.» «Yo también. Casi no podía mantener los ojos abiertos en el tren.»
teaching.explanationEs: So + auxiliar + sujeto = yo también. El auxiliar es el de la frase original: am.
segments: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I
could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”
teaching.audioText: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”

teaching.en: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”
teaching.es: «Anoche no dormí muy bien.» «Yo tampoco. Los vecinos estuvieron gritando hasta casi las tres.»
teaching.explanationEs: Neither + auxiliar + sujeto = yo tampoco; el auxiliar copia didn't y el verbo se omite.
segments: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did
I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”
teaching.audioText: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”

teaching.en: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”
teaching.es: «¿Estarán despejadas las carreteras cuando salgamos?» «Eso espero. El pronóstico dice que la nieve parará antes del mediodía.»
teaching.explanationEs: So sustituye a toda la oración (the roads will be clear). En negativo: I hope not.
segments: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I
hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”
teaching.audioText: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”

teaching.en: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”
teaching.es: «¿Estará Tom ocupado toda la tarde?» «Me temo que sí, y más bien dudo que tenga tiempo para nosotros antes de las seis.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid so / not da una mala noticia con educación y sustituye a toda la oración.
segments: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and
I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”
teaching.audioText: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”

teaching.en: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”
teaching.es: «¿Nos lo saltamos esta noche?» «Preferiría que no. Estoy totalmente de acuerdo en que estamos rendidos, pero se ofenderían.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather not omite el verbo de la propuesta (give it a miss). I couldn't agree more refuerza un acuerdo.
segments: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I
couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”
teaching.audioText: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué se omite tras «I'd love to» en la respuesta de Leo?

choices.text: help his cousin move
have a few friends over
phone her at six
stay for dinner afterwards

feedback.es: I'd love to deja solo to: el verbo omitido es el de la pregunta de Mia (stay for dinner afterwards). Lo demás son otros datos del texto.

hint.es: Busca el verbo de la pregunta de Mia: es lo que Leo no repite.

origin.text: Mia phoned Leo at six: “We're having a few friends over tomorrow. Would you like to stay for dinner afterwards?” “I'd love to,” said Leo, “but I'm afraid I've promised to help my cousin move.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Yo también. Llevamos en la carretera desde las seis.»

feedback.es: La frase original es afirmativa (I'm exhausted), así que se usa so + am + I; neither exigiría una frase negativa.

hint.es: Frase afirmativa: «yo también» con el auxiliar am.

origin.text: “I'm absolutely exhausted after the drive.” “___ am I. We've been on the road since six, after all.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Espero que sí, pero me temo que el pronóstico dice lo contrario.»

answer.text: I hope so, but I'm afraid the forecast says otherwise

feedback.es: I hope so sustituye a toda la oración y I'm afraid introduce una mala noticia con cortesía: suavizan el contraste.

hint.es: Primero la esperanza (so), después el but con la mala noticia.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada réplica elíptica con lo que significa.

pairs: “I've never been to Lisbon.” “Neither have I.”
“Are you coming on Friday?” “I'd love to.”

pairs.es: Me temo que no está abierta

feedback.es: Cada réplica omite lo dicho antes: neither have I copia have, I'd love to deja to, not sustituye a la oración y so does copia does.

pairs: “I've never been to Lisbon.” “Neither have I.”
“Are you coming on Friday?” “I'd love to.”

pairs.es: Me temo que no está abierta

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pasa con Mia y con Leo según Sara.

choices.text: Both are busy with the same deadline.
Mia is free but Leo is not.
Neither of them has been invited.
Both will come if Sara does.

feedback.es: I'm afraid not responde a «Will Mia be free?» y so does Leo copia el verbo has: los dos tienen la misma fecha límite.

origin.audio: Carlos invited Sara to a concert on Friday. “I'd love to,” she said, “but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work.” “Will Mia be free, then?” he asked. “I'm afraid not. She has the same deadline, and so does Leo.” Carlos laughed. “Then I'll give it a miss too.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia tampoco lo vio, hasta donde sé, así que quizá no fue.»

feedback.es: La frase original es negativa y en pasado (didn't see): neither copia el auxiliar did e invierte el orden con el sujeto.

origin.text: “Did you see Tom at the wedding?” “No, I didn't. Neither ___ Mia, as far as I know, so he may not have gone at all.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir Ana con «I'm afraid not».

choices.text: That Carlos has not replied to the invitation yet.
That Carlos will not be coming.
That Carlos would come if Sara did.
That Carlos was never actually invited.

feedback.es: I'm afraid not sustituye a toda la respuesta (Carlos will not come) y la razón llega justo después: está desbordado de trabajo.

origin.audio: By Thursday, the replies to Ana's invitations had started to arrive. “Will Carlos come?” asked Mia. “I'm afraid not,” said Ana. “He's swamped, and so is Sara.” “Well, I'd love to help with the food,” said Mia, “but I'm exhausted after the week I've had.” “Neither of us has slept much,” Ana admitted. “I hope Leo will say yes, at least.” “I hope so too,” said Mia. “He'd rather not sit at home alone, and he never declines an invitation from you.” Ana smiled. “I couldn't agree more,” she said. “Honestly, it would not feel like a party without him.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué se deduce del cambio de opinión de Mia en estos mensajes?

choices.text: That she had never wanted to go to Tom's house.
That she was offended that Tom asked Sara first.
That she mainly wanted to go because of her friends.
That she had suddenly remembered another plan.

feedback.es: Mia acepta con I'd love to, pero se echa atrás al saber que Sara y Carlos no irán: lo que le interesaba era la compañía. El texto no menciona ofensa ni otro plan.

origin.text: Tom's text to Mia read: “Dinner at mine on Saturday?” Mia replied: “I'd love to. Will Sara be there?” “I'm afraid not,” wrote Tom. “She's tied up all weekend. Neither will Carlos, I gather.” Mia's answer took an hour: “Mm. I'd rather not, then. Count me out this time.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que no. Cerró a las cuatro, así que tendrás que ir mañana.»

feedback.es: I'm afraid not sustituye a la oración negativa (it isn't open); I'm afraid so contradiría la razón que se da después.

origin.text: “Is the bank still open?” “I'm afraid ___. It closed at four, so you'll have to go tomorrow.”

prompt.es: Ordena a «I've never enjoyed big weddings»: «Yo tampoco, y prefiero no ir a más.»

answer.text: Neither have I, and I would rather not go to another

feedback.es: Neither have I copia el auxiliar de I've never enjoyed; después, would rather not + verbo base expresa la preferencia.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el propósito principal de esta nota de Sara?

choices.text: To ask Mia to move the reception to another week.
To apologise for having missed an earlier celebration.
To offer her help as a condition for attending.
To decline the invitation while keeping the friendship warm.

feedback.es: La nota rechaza con cortesía: empieza con calidez, da una razón y ofrece ayuda. No pide cambiar la fecha ni condiciona su asistencia.

origin.text: Dear Mia, thank you for the invitation to your wedding reception. I would love to come, and I'm touched that you asked me. Unfortunately, I will be tied up with work that week, and I'm afraid I can't change it. I do hope you understand. Please give my love to Tom, and let me know if there is anything I can do in the meantime.

prompt.es: Escucha y deduce qué sospecha Ana sobre el informe.

choices.text: That it may still contain errors nobody has found.
That Tom refused to write the sales section.
That the client has already rejected an earlier draft.
That Leo wants to avoid working at the weekend.

feedback.es: I hope so deja ver que Leo no está seguro, y neither has Tom añade que tampoco nadie más revisó las cifras: Ana teme errores sin detectar.

origin.audio: “Is the report ready to send?” asked Ana. “I hope so,” said Leo, “but I haven't checked the figures yet.” Ana looked worried. “Neither has Tom, as far as I know, and he wrote the sales section.” “Then I'd rather not send it today,” said Leo. “Let's wait until Monday.” “I couldn't agree more,” said Ana. “We can't afford a mistake in front of the client.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Tuve que rechazar la invitación porque estaba desbordado de trabajo.»

feedback.es: Decline an invitation es la colocación educada para rechazar; refuse y turn down también son posibles, aunque más directos.

origin.text: Mia asked whether I would like to join them in the mountains for the weekend, but I was swamped with work, so I had to ___ the invitation.
